notes.title: WW2 survival game reinvents itself, turns to Witcher writers for "darker" story
notes.content:
You may remember War Mechanic from its reveal last year. It looked like a fairly standard survival game with an interesting alt-history premise. World War 2 never ended, and now the war is fought with robots by your side as the military has been privatized. However, after a quiet year, developer Chronospace has reimagined the game to take on a whole new lease of life. New writers are on board to soup up the narrative and new mechanics are involved to make the gameplay more exciting. It's basically a whole new game.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Weather on Nordhook
notes.content:
[p]In this devlog, we’ll discuss how the time of day and weather influence[b] the missions in Nordhook[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/1f273252531e30a15afe0ec9b8f5d89480d9cb47.gif"][/img][/p][p]The time of day and weather will be integral to every mission, giving each one its unique mood and challenges. We don’t plan to include a fully dynamic system, but every scenario is carefully designed with specific conditions.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/40badbb57124e98f3c5fe3075081d646aaff43b2.gif"][/img][/p][p]Some missions will take place in broad daylight, while others will occur during a sunrise or an atmospheric sunset. And sometimes you’ll move under the cover of deep night, where silence, darkness, and the right equipment are essential to get the job done.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/cf0fab2538dcaaad117935617af073204c79f9a8.gif"][/img][/p][p]Weather adds another layer of variety. From fog hiding dangers in the distance, through pouring rain and violent storms, to clear skies — each setting changes how you approach the task.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/43049e7fbd839a9f808934ee4e1a57970de2d34e.gif"][/img][/p][p]The combination of time and weather means that every mission offers not just a different look, but also a new tactical challenge.

Stay tuned for more.
Chronospace Team.[/p][p][/p][p][url="https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/chronospace/war-mechanic-explore-repair-automate" style="button" buttoncolor="#816b1d"]KICKSTARTER[/url] - PRE-LUNCH PAGE[/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/ByqnPE7bwZ " style="button" buttoncolor="#184272"]DISCORD[/url] - JOIN OUR COMMUNITY[/p]

notes.title: Upgrade or Die
notes.content:
[h1][b]GUNS, UPGRADES, WORKBENCH[/b][/h1][p][/p][p][b]Ready to turn scrap into pure firepower?[/b][/p][p]In War Mechanic, weapons are your best friends, your loudest allies, and sometimes your only ticket out alive. The right grip, sight, or magazine can mean the difference between profit... and a body bag.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/f6f58f8c011e9ca510060a32524b254d9f41275d.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Let’s dive into how you can craft, tweak, and dominate the battlefield with style.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/9c970b34ab4d884ea2237762e4acf857767ad8a8.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Workbench Mechanics[/b][/p][p]The workbench is an essential tool for every player. This is where you can modify and upgrade your weapons, tailoring them to your personal needs and playstyle. In the workshop, you’ll craft unique gear that will help you survive even the toughest battles. To perform upgrades, you’ll need specific resources and blueprints, which can be found during missions, purchased from Wild Bill, or discovered while exploring the island.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/09acf9d51b08858d2a05e9f0778cb3f76b86e69e.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Upgrade Process[/b][/p][p]To upgrade a weapon, players need to collect enough resources (such as metals, electronic components, and mechanical parts) used to craft new parts. Blueprints are essential for each upgrade - they provide detailed instructions for making modifications correctly.[/p][p]Every upgrade requires careful planning and the right materials. This process is crucial for adapting your arsenal to the game’s increasing difficulty.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/00842316f1c6e8e92124d5b86b99a7640a5d5098.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b]Weapon Upgrades:[/b][/p][p]At the workbench, you can modify the following weapon parts:[/p][list][*][p][b]Grip[/b]: Improves stability, accuracy, and handling. A better grip means less recoil and more precise shots.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Optics[/b]: Swap scopes, holographic sights, or red dot sights to improve aiming speed, precision, and adaptability in different combat scenarios.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Bolt[/b]: Upgrading the bolt increases reload speed, firing stability, and weapon durability.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Trigger[/b]: A better trigger enhances responsiveness and firing rate, enabling faster and more accurate shots.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/3f908a4d90e54842de22029f2b1de2d73ca93da1.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/811eea51b3a8e90eb3ee08997e58da5b9be98736.jpg"][/img][/p][list][*][p][b]Magazine[/b]: Expanding magazine capacity means longer bursts without reloading, which is crucial in intense firefights.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Attachments[/b]: Add accessories like suppressors, foregrips, lasers, or side rails to gain tactical advantages and improve weapon versatility. You’ll need to install the top and bottom rails first: the top rail for optics and the bottom rail for other attachments.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/1c9093f287b95cbb04f76d7f7d195f236a509120.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]Weapon examples:[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Shotgun[/b] — devastating at close range. Perfect for quickly breaking shields or clearing crowds. Can be upgraded for a tighter spread or boosted damage with special ammo.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Pistol[/b] — a versatile choice with fast aiming. Great for taking out single targets, can be customized for rapid critical hits or silent takedowns.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Revolver[/b] — high penetration and precision. Excellent for hitting weak spots, favored by players who enjoy a close-range “sniper” style.[/p][/*][*][p][b]SMG[/b] — rapid-fire weapon ideal for on-the-move combat. At higher levels, it can acquire status effects such as bleeding or disorientation.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/d11216e329fd0365904d400d1b54380748ab983d.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Combat is all about analysis and precision: it’s not just about shooting — you need to know where to hit, what to hit with, and how to upgrade your arsenal to survive.[/p][p][b]Every enemy in War Mechanic has weak points you’ll need to learn to target, such as. Study your targets. Adapt your loadout.[/b][/p][list][*][p]Exposed energy cores[/p][/*][*][p]Sensory modules (eyes, cameras)[/p][/*][*][p]Unarmored joints[/p][/*][*][p]Overheated armor sections[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/3c5530819133ee30c802154d90960e8b1fa7eb1a.gif"][/img][/p][p]
That’s just a taste — we’ll be showing much more very soon.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/14f37e4059098ae9724a8fbfc7f4959270c8c75e.gif"][/img][/p][p]We’ll be sharing even more soon – but in the meantime, you can [b]visit our Kickstarter preview[/b].[/p][p]It’s your chance to take an early look, share your thoughts, and get ready to be part of the War Mechanic journey from the very start![/p][p][/p][p][url="https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/chronospace/war-mechanic-explore-repair-automate?ref=nav_search&result=project&term=war%20mechanic&total_hits=26" style="button" buttoncolor="#7f7610"]Kickstarter Preview[/url][/p]

notes.title: A letter from Patton - dev update about War Mechanic
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/8cd969a3da80a8240f6b4f8af59597a282072f18.png[/img]

While you read the letter from General Patton himself, please take a moment to update yourself on the latest developments in our game - War Mechanic!

Just over two months ago, we released the trailer for "War Mechanic." We received a lot of feedback from you—so much, in fact, that we needed some time to process it all. There was an overwhelming amount of praise for our efforts, but just as much valuable input on what could be improved. Thanks for all that! Patton would say that no project can be successful without full dedication, so we treat your feedback seriously!

First, let's start with the most important information: we are postponing the release. To ensure War Mechanic meets all the highest standards and provides the best possible experience at launch, we’ve decided to invest more time and additional efforts in strengthening our unique game concept.

So now, to the real stuff, what have we been up to lately? 

[h1]Meet Jack Wallace - the War Mechanic[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/f47003bdf6bd086db3197e12bba3e2d6b46a3c4b.jpg[/img]

The first huge change you can find on the “War Mechanic” Steam page is the introduction of new models of the main character of the game, Jack Wallace. 
The fate of the war depends on this bearded badass's actions. Win this war and show the USSR how U.S. mechanics work.

[h1]Gizmo - your mechanical sidekick[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/5f6c78a3f25a7cb833d2f2ae5446ac70adbefd8f.png[/img]

Every hero needs an assistant; Batman had Robin, Don Quixote had Sancho, and you have Gizmo! This rusty old robot (check out his past; there are some well-hidden secrets buried deep under his rusted helmet) will help you learn all the basic mechanics of the game. During the game, you will have the opportunity to discover his past, secrets hidden deep on his hard drive. Knowing his secrets, will you look at him the same way as before? Does the term - Wunder Waffe tell you anything?

[h1]Welcome to Garage![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/a1ec777cd0a13484bec1a87133b96e735d7d7f36.gif[/img]

Exploring Nordhook is essential for collecting unique materials, blueprints, and upgrades for the base. It’s often too risky to go on foot; the sun is blazing, the distances are long, and you never know what strange stuff the Nazis and Soviets left behind! 

You will soon discover this rugged old light military vehicle, left to rust in one of the base facilities. If you take care of it and invest time and resources, you can transform this pile of scrap into a real old-timer hot rod! 

As the game progresses, you will be able to upgrade it, both mechanically and visually. In addition, you have to monitor the fuel level and vehicle efficiency and constantly repair it, and it will serve you for many years of war.

[h1]Blaster - melt to collect[/h1]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/bf6cf20e7497947ab58eca8fcd8f45d81098a786.png[/img]

The island is littered with wrecks. Cleaning up the debris provides all the materials to complete the contracts—that’s why you need a dependable tool like the Hand Blaster, which can cut through scrap of any size.

We are preparing interesting updates about the blaster and other core mechanics of the game in a series called “Nordhook Diaries”. Wishlist the game so you won’t miss it!

[h1]Workshop - help to push the front![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45242932/2ff4d25b45271c14238aafb7bf97f97e752b5877.gif[/img]

In War Mechanic, one of the key elements of the game is repairing destroyed military vehicles to assist your allies on the front lines.

Repairs are conducted in a special building known as the post-Nazi Workshop. All vehicles, whether cars or tanks, are transported by a massive train that comes directly from the war front.

At the start of the game, your task will be to manually repair all vehicles, from diagnosing damage to disassembling and repairing parts and finally to reassembling them. As the game progresses, you will begin using robots for this purpose. Keep in mind, they never get tired!

Godspeed, gentleman!

notes.title: Dieselpunk in War Mechanic - DEVLOG#1
notes.content:
[h2]Hey everyone![/h2] We've always been fascinated by dieselpunk - not just as a style, but as a complete alternative vision of technology. Imagine a world driven by mechanical ingenuity, where problems are solved with engineering rather than microprocessors. That's the world we're building.

We are currently focusing on the vehicle you'll be driving. Our art team has put a lot of effort into designing this mechanical beast - every component has its purpose. You'll need to upgrade it as you progress through the game, making it essential for overcoming new challenges.

We just wrapped up work on an abandoned industrial complex, and our first test drives through this space were incredibly rewarding—it’s exactly the vibe we were aiming for.

Looking ahead, we’re all about refining the core gameplay experience. We want the vehicle handling, exploration, and shooting of aircraft to feel as satisfying as possible. The world looks the part; now we’re making sure it’s a blast to play.

[h3]Get a glimpse of our concept art and immerse yourself in the world of War Mechanic.[/h3]

notes.title: World War II still rages on in alternate history simulation game War Mechanic
notes.content:
The horrors of World War II have been long chronicled in the annals of videogame history, from all-out war games like Call of Duty and Battlefield to more strategic offerings such as Hearts of Iron and Brothers in Arms, or cerebral, story-led experiences including Valiant Hearts and This War of Mine. War Mechanic, however, imagines an alternate history where the Second World War instead escalated into open conflict between the Soviet Union and the United States, and tasks you with surviving in its retro-inspired dieselpunk reality.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Chronospace Unveils War Mechanic: Ready To Win The War?
notes.content: Chronospace has announced War Mechanic, a unique first-person sim set in a dieselpunk world, arriving on PC in 2025. Coming to PC in 2025, Chronospace has announced War Mechanic, a first-person sim set in a dieselpunk world where players take on the role of a military base manager and mechanic in an alternate reality where World War II has escalated into open conflict with the Soviet Union and the rest of the free world. The game will feature strategy elements, resource management, base building and defence, alongside exploration and a fleshed-out narrative. War Mechanic offers a retro-inspired aesthetic, a sense of humour, and sharp satire. Stepping into the world of War Mechanic, World War II evolves into a conflict between the Soviet Union and the United States, with both sides focusing on the development of robots and acquiring Nazi technology. However, Soviet sabotage leads to the detonation of atomic charges at Los Alamos, killing the president, vice president, cabinet members, and key Manhattan Project scientists. Following this tragedy, General Patton wins the accelerated presidential election and declares war on the USSR.
